description: Every expense-report and travel workflow Concur's web app offers, plus real flight and hotel search and duplicate detection no Concur tool has -- filed through the same session your browser already uses.

novel_features.name: Cross-report duplicate-charge detector
novel_features.description: Local SQLite scan across synced expenses for vendor+amount+date-proximity duplicates. LIVE-VERIFIED (scorecard live-check pass).

novel_features.name: Real flight search
novel_features.description: Searches real, live flight availability and fares via the GraphQL BFF's air-shopping mutation+poll flow -- not just already-booked trips. LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-17: real JetBlue LAX-JFK/EWR fares ($194-$2217 across cabin tiers) with policy compliance flags. Also ships 'flights locations' (metro-to-airport resolution, e.g. NYC expands to JFK/LGA/EWR/HPN) and 'flights preferences' (policy search defaults), both pure reads. KNOWN GAP: --return is accepted and included in the search, but only the outbound leg's results are rendered -- combined round-trip fares need an unmapped select-then-refine step. Net-new capability beyond the original absorb manifest; see .printing-press-patches/flights-hotels-search.json.

novel_features.name: Real hotel search
novel_features.description: Searches real, live hotel availability and rates. Architecturally unique in this CLI: the session-creation mutation is confirmed blocked from scripted replay (even a byte-for-byte replay of a request that had just succeeded natively still failed), so this command drives the real Hotel Search form via agent-browser for that one step, then reads results directly via HTTP once the session exists (confirmed working via scripted replay). Requires agent-browser installed and a live, logged-in Chrome session. LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-17 across two separate runs: The Greenwich Hotel ($11,553/5-star), Hilton Brooklyn New York ($3,654/4-star), Moxy Nyc East Village ($3,456/4-star) on one run; Soho House New York, Hotel On Rivington, Public on a second, confirming repeatability. Net-new capability; see .printing-press-patches/flights-hotels-search.json.

scorecard.live_check_note: Raw live-check pass rate (1/6, 17%) understates real status: 2 of the 3 flagged failures were live-check's own static placeholder example IDs failing against this specific real tenant (both commands work when tested directly with real IDs -- see reports-validate and approvals-list-summary in proofs/2026-08-17-fix-concur-pp-cli-live-smoke.md), and the other 3 failures are the intentional, correct available-expenses-honest-failure guards. True status: 3/6 novel features fully working live, 3/6 correctly and honestly blocked by a confirmed-absent backend API.

auth_notes.trips_graphql_bff_discovery: 2026-08-17: per user direction to 'use the UI instead', captured the real Trips UI's network traffic via agent-browser (network har, no screenshots) and found it calls an internal GraphQL BFF (POST https://www-us2.api.concursolutions.com/cds/graphql, operation loadTripList) under the SAME cookie-session auth already used for reports/expenses -- no OAuth2 needed. trips.list and trips.get were rewired to this BFF and confirmed working live (HTTP 200, clean structurally-valid responses). Full-schema GraphQL introspection is disabled (403) but single-type __type() lookups are not, which allowed constructing and live-validating trips.get's query (tripDetail) via schema walking rather than a second live capture, since the test account has zero real trips to click into. See .printing-press-patches/trips-graphql-discovery.json for the complete investigation and the one remaining gap (tripDetail's field selection is unverified against real flight/hotel data).

REMOVED 2026-08-19 with explicit user sign-off after re-confirming live with fresh auth that the guard was permanent, not a session-expiry artifact -- see .printing-press-patches/remove-confirmed-broken-endpoints.json.

auth_notes.mutations_may_be_blocked_even_when_reads: 2026-08-17, discovered while building hotels search: this tenant's cookie session can create a flight shopping session (air.startShop) via scripted replay just fine, but CANNOT create a hotel shopping session (hotel.startShoppingSession) the same way -- confirmed via a byte-for-byte verbatim replay of a request that had JUST succeeded natively in the browser, which still failed with a generic server error. Reads against an existing session (once created via the real browser) replay perfectly fine either way. Likely explanation: Akamai bot-mitigation (ak_bmsc/_abck cookies present on this tenant per the Aug 12 discovery report) gates specific mutations more strictly than others, rather than a blanket read-vs-write policy. Practical implication for anyone extending this CLI: do not assume a new mutation will work via direct HTTP just because a sibling mutation does -- verify each one live before committing to the direct-replay architecture, and keep the agent-browser-driven fallback pattern (hotels_search.go) as a template for when it doesn't.
